BIOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #12
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: BIOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----

   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Burning crop residue every week

   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Taxonomy II ● Kingdom Plantae (general characteristics of organisms in Divisions.

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

5. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Ice melting to water

7. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in Animals ● External fertilisation in animals ● Types of internal ? (1 mark)

   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Nitrogen gas only

   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. newton (N)
   C. watt (W)
   D. joule (J)

13. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

14. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Primary consumers only
